tasks.title: ngv2/report.py — deterministic report builder + markdown renderer
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/report.py exists and imports VERDICTS from ngv2.contracts (no re-definition of VERDICTS, Finding, LiveTestReport, or HuntState).
build_report(state, reports) returns a dict with EXACTLY the keys 'phase', 'findings', 'results', 'summary' (no extra keys).
report['phase'] == state.phase; report['findings'] == [f.to_dict() for f in state.findings]; report['results'] == [r.to_dict() for r in reports].
report['summary'] has one count per VERDICTS member — 'confirmed', 'refuted', 'error', 'inconclusive' — each equal to the number of reports whose .verdict equals that value.
render_markdown(report) returns a str that STARTS with '#'.
render_markdown(report) contains every finding's title and target text, and contains every result's verdict text (e.g. 'confirmed' appears for a confirmed result).

Module is pure and stdlib-only: no I/O, file access, subprocess, socket, or network; no eval/exec/__import__; no module-level globals (beyond the import) and no randomness; the only public symbols are build_report and render_markdown.
tests/test_report.py is NOT created or modified; `python -m pytest tests/test_report.py -q` passes.

spec.objective: Implement the NEW pure, deterministic, stdlib-only file ngv2/report.py exposing build_report(state, reports) -> dict and render_markdown(report: dict) -> str, satisfying the already-committed oracle tests/test_report.py, by reading the imported VERDICTS and calling the supplied objects' .to_dict() — without re-implementing any dataclass.
functional_requirements: Create NEW file ngv2/report.py that imports VERDICTS from ngv2.contracts and uses only the Python standard library; do NOT import any other Epic-2 child module (grounding, poc_runner, pipeline) and do NOT re-define Finding, LiveTestReport, HuntState, or VERDICTS.
build_report(state, reports) returns a dict whose key set is EXACTLY {'phase', 'findings', 'results', 'summary'} with no additional keys.

build_report sets report['phase'] = state.phase, report['findings'] = [f.to_dict() for f in state.findings], and report['results'] = [r.to_dict() for r in reports], preserving input order and calling .to_dict() on each object rather than introspecting fields.
build_report adds, for each verdict v in VERDICTS, report['summary'][v] = number of reports r where r.verdict == v (covering 'confirmed', 'refuted', 'error', 'inconclusive').
render_markdown(report) returns a string whose first character is '#' (a top-level markdown header).
render_markdown renders, for each finding in report['findings'], a section that CONTAINS that finding's title and target text.
render_markdown renders each result's verdict text from report['results'] (e.g. a result with verdict 'confirmed' yields a section containing the word 'confirmed').

render_markdown consumes ONLY the dict produced by build_report (never live state/report objects), and the module is deterministic and pure: no I/O, subprocess, socket, network, eval/exec/__import__, mutable module-level globals, or randomness, and exposes no public symbols beyond build_report and render_markdown.
spec.interfaces: from ngv2.contracts import VERDICTS; build_report(state, reports) -> dict  # {'phase': state.phase, 'findings': [f.to_dict() ...], 'results': [r.to_dict() ...], 'summary': {'total_findings': int, 'confirmed': int, 'refuted': int, 'error': int, 'inconclusive': int}}; render_markdown(report: dict) -> str  # starts with '#', contains each finding's title/target and each result's verdict text
edge_cases: Empty state.findings and empty reports: build_report returns total_findings=0 and 0 for every verdict count; render_markdown still starts with '#' and does not error.
reports containing verdict values not in VERDICTS (if any): they are simply not counted in the summary and do not create new summary keys.
Multiple reports sharing the same verdict are counted cumulatively.
Findings whose to_dict() title/target contain markdown-significant characters must still appear verbatim enough that the substring checks for title and target succeed.
Verdict counts must use exact equality on r.verdict (no case-folding or partial match).
non_goals: Do NOT author, create, or modify any test file; tests/test_report.py is already committed.
Do NOT perform any I/O, file access, subprocess, socket, or network operations.
Do NOT use eval, exec, or __import__; no randomness or mutable module-level globals.
Do NOT re-implement or redefine Finding, LiveTestReport, HuntState, or VERDICTS.
Do NOT add fields, public functions, dict keys, or symbols beyond build_report and render_markdown, and do NOT change their names, signatures, dict keys, or return shapes.
Do NOT import or depend on any other Epic-2 child module (grounding, poc_runner, pipeline).
spec.implementation_notes: Read VERDICTS from ngv2.contracts and iterate it to build the per-verdict counts so the summary stays in lock-step with the contract tuple ('confirmed','refuted','error','inconclusive'). Build the summary as {'total_findings': len(state.findings)} then add counts via something like {v: sum(1 for r in reports if r.verdict == v) for v in VERDICTS}. build_report should call obj.to_dict() for findings and reports rather than reading private fields. render_markdown should read only the returned dict: start the string with a top-level '#' header, then for each entry in report['findings'] emit a section including the finding dict's title and target values, and for each entry in report['results'] include its verdict value as text. Keep output deterministic (no dict-ordering surprises — iterate lists in order). Confirm against the committed oracle with `python -m pytest tests/test_report.py -q`.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: HuntState-like stub with .phase (str) and .findings (list of Finding-like objects each exposing .to_dict() returning a mapping with 'title' and 'target'); list of LiveTestReport-like objects constructed as LiveTestReport(poc_finding_id, verdict, exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms) each exposing .verdict and .to_dict(); coverage of every VERDICTS value, empty lists, duplicate verdicts, and an out-of-VERDICTS verdict. These fixtures are supplied by the already-committed tests/test_report.py; this task authors no new tests.

token_budget_ratio.note: IMPL-ONLY: no new tests are authored (oracle tests/test_report.py is committed). The test_tokens reflect the effort to read/understand the committed oracle and verify behavior against it, kept >= 1.5x implementation per schema.
